name: list_tags
title: List assignable tags
description:
List existing tag ids, names and descriptions in name order. complete:false means the hub catalog has not arrived. Descriptions guide LLMs on when to apply a tag. Reuse existing meanings and apply only tags that improve discovery; leaving a document untagged is valid. Use create_tag for missing categories and edit_tag to explicitly change usage guidance.

Help: list_tags, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: create_tag
title: Create or reuse a tag

name.description: Trimmed and lowercased before validation: at most 30 lowercase letters/digits with single hyphens between groups.

description.description: Guidance for LLMs on when to apply the tag: one line, at most 300 characters after trimming.

description:
Explicitly create a missing workspace catalog tag. Read list_tags and check complete first; an incomplete catalog can hide an existing or deleted name. Reuse existing meanings and keep the vocabulary small: create only reusable subjects or purposes, avoiding synonyms and one-off task, file, issue or version tags. Apply only tags that improve discovery; leaving a document untagged is valid. Names are trimmed and lowercased. An existing normalized name returns its canonical entry without changing its description; use edit_tag for that. Descriptions guide LLMs on when to apply the tag. Creation assigns no documents and retains Workspace settings permissions and offline recovery; local workspaces need no hub or sign-in.

Help: create_tag, list_tags, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: edit_tag
title: Edit a tag's usage guidance

id.description: Existing catalog tag id from list_tags; aliases resolve to the canonical entry.

description.description: Guidance for LLMs on when to apply the tag: one line, at most 300 characters after trimming; null or blank clears it.

description:
Explicitly replace an existing tag's description as guidance for LLMs on when to apply it. Read list_tags and check complete first, then use an existing id and keep its meaning. Keeps the name, identity and document assignments; never creates tags. Null or blank clears the description; an identical edit has no further effect. Reuse a small vocabulary of subjects or purposes; avoid synonyms and one-off task, file, issue or version tags. Use the guidance to select tags only when they improve discovery; a document may remain untagged. Retains Workspace settings permissions and offline recovery; local workspaces need no hub or sign-in.

Help: edit_tag, list_tags, create_tag, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: create_doc
title: Create a document

title.description: Display title; identity is the document's UUID, never this. Required except on a decision successor. A decision topic has one title, stored on its first record and naming the question rather than the answer; a successor omits title or repeats that exact title.

description.description: Read only by agents, never shown to people: whatever best helps an agent find this document with list_docs and search and decide whether to open it. A keyword list is fine.

tldr.description: One or two sentences of plain English for a person opening a regular document. At most 300 characters; null clears it. Decisions have no TL;DR.

answer.description: Record a person's answer, not the agent's own approval; MCP does not verify its provenance. Accepted only with `kind: decision`.

when.description: When the person gave the answer: an ISO 8601 date-time with a time zone, e.g. 2026-10-24T10:55:00Z. Pass the current time if the answer was given just now.

where.description: Where the answer was given, such as a conversation or review URL.

tags.description: Existing catalog tag ids or names, case ignored. An unknown or deleted tag refuses before anything is created.

kind.description: The document's record kind. Omit it for an ordinary working document.

status.description: The initial lifecycle state. Accepted only with `kind: decision`.

related.description: One live, locally readable regular document UUID or a non-empty list of them. The related set is fixed at creation. Omitted successors inherit their predecessor's whole set; supplying related replaces it. Accepted only with `kind: decision`.

discussion.description: Live, locally readable regular document UUID holding this record's RFC discussion. Accepted only with `kind: decision`; never inherited. Correct or clear with set_metadata only while open; fixed after leaving open. Does not create or tag a document.

supersedes.description: Earlier decision UUID this new decision replaces. Immutable and accepted only with `kind: decision`.

text.description: Plain prose (`inline` supplies formatting), literal code/terminal/chart source, exactly one GFM table, or :::card/:::figma content without delimiters. See markdown help for cell formatting, container keys, buttons and links. Invalid content refuses with invalid_table, invalid_card or invalid_figma before writing.

language.description: Code language, e.g. "ts". Code blocks only. Drawings are code blocks too, with language "ablauf" or "wireframe".

list.description: List style. List items only; omitted means bullet.

indent.description: List depth, an integer from 0 to 3. List items only; omitted means 0.

variant.description: Callout variant: note, tip, important, warning or caution; omitted means note. Ignored for other block types.

icon.description: Callout icon override: one emoji character or a curated :name: icon. Ignored for other block types.

inline.description: Prose (paragraph, heading, list-item, quote, callout) runs `[{text, marks}]`: marks are bold, italic, strike, inlineCode, link (external http(s) URL) or docLink (document UUID). Replaces `text` with joined run texts. Code, terminal and chart ignore it and use literal `text`; tables, cards and figma ignore it and parse inline Markdown from `text` (one GFM table or content inside :::card/:::figma). Empty docLink text takes the target's current title. A target unknown to this replica's directory refuses with doclink_target_not_known_locally before writing; archived targets are accepted.

sidebar.description: Optional sidebar placement. Omitted, the document is created unpinned — alive and reachable, simply not an entry point.

id.description: An EXISTING group's id, as get_sidebar returns it. Never a name: an unknown id fails the call.

position.description: Position in the group, clamped into range. Omitted means last.

description:
Create a regular page or a decision record, optionally with starting blocks, tags, a TL;DR (regular pages only) and a sidebar pin. A description is always required, and so is a title except on a decision successor, which takes its topic's title. Every reference (tags, related pages, supersedes, discussion and sidebar group) is checked before anything is written, so a refusal creates nothing. A decision is created open or decided: deciding needs supported answer blocks and no TL;DR or data, and a decided successor also needs a recorded person's answer. The document, directory and sidebar are separate writes; if one fails, persistence_failed names the completed rooms and gives a recovery that cannot create a duplicate.

Help: create_doc, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown.

name: get_doc
title: Read a document
description:
Read live metadata, blocks with edit-assertion rev hashes, table column_widths, comment threads and decision context. Creation time createdAt and decision entries' createdAt/updatedAt are ISO 8601 UTC strings when known and representable. Data lists collections/counts; use get_data for records. Use get_revision for a historical state.

Help: get_doc, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown, data.

name: list_revisions
title: List document revisions

refresh.description: Revalidate the catalog through the hub before answering; use after an unknown naming or restore outcome. Requires a connection.

description:
List this computer's cached revision catalog newest first, including archived documents, with cache freshness. Missing history downloads when connected; cached reads work offline. Use refresh: true to check an unknown mutation outcome. IDs work with get_revision/get_data/restore_revision. Empty means a complete downloaded catalog has no history. Listing a decision record refuses with decision_no_history.

Help: list_revisions, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: name_revision
title: Name the current document revision

name.description: The name the person requested, from 1 to 100 characters on one line.

description:
Name the current synchronized state only when a person asks. Requires team-hub write access; closes its stretch. One name per revision; manage it in the web. Naming a decision record refuses with decision_no_history.

Help: name_revision, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: restore_revision
title: Restore a document revision

revision.description: A hub revision id from list_revisions.

description:
Restore title, blocks and data from a hub revision as a new revision. Requires synchronized write access to a live document; history and other metadata stay. An identical state writes nothing. Restoring a decision record refuses with decision_no_history.

Help: restore_revision, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: get_revision
title: Read a document revision

revision.description: Hub revision ID from this document's cached list_revisions catalog; distinct from get_doc's page and block rev hashes. Historical reads use downloaded snapshots, fetching missing snapshots when connected.

description:
Read a cached revision from list_revisions: title, visible blocks without rev, data summary and cache freshness. Missing snapshots download when connected; downloaded history works offline. Archived documents work. Page records with get_data and the same revision. Reading a decision record's revision refuses with decision_no_history.

Help: get_revision, workspaces, tool-contracts, data.

name: get_data
title: Read document data

revision.description: Hub revision ID from this document's cached list_revisions catalog; distinct from get_doc's page and block rev hashes. Historical reads use downloaded snapshots, fetching missing snapshots when connected.

collection.description: Collection name; omit for the area summary.

limit.description: Records per page, 0 for the schema only; needs collection.

max_bytes.description: Page record budget in bytes; needs collection.

ids.description: Only these record ids; needs collection.

description:
Read a data summary, or name collection for bounded records and diagnostics. limit: 0 reads schema; follow next_after until complete. Optional revision reads this computer's cached snapshot using an ID from list_revisions, fetching it when connected if missing, including archived documents; omission reads live data. Live data and open revisions can change between calls. Historical decision data refuses with decision_no_history.

Help: get_data, workspaces, tool-contracts, data.

name: update_data
title: Update document data

schema.description: Raw versioned collection schema, validated by applyDocData.

description:
Apply one validated batch of changes to a document's structured data, naming each touched collection once. Within a collection the steps run in order: set `schema`, optionally `replaceRecords`, then `deleteRecords`, then `upsert` whole `{id, value}` records; `deleteCollection: true` excludes other changes. Schema and value JSON are validated as sent, and unsupported schemas or invalid retained records refuse before anything changes. The batch is one local transaction; an identical refresh returns `changed: false` without writing. The result summarizes touched collections, record counts and deletions with durability, without values.

Refresh producer-owned collections by upsert or full-set replacement, and keep human dispositions in a separate collection keyed by producer record ids. Split changes above the 1 MiB schema/value budget across calls; separate calls are not atomic together and offer no compare-and-swap or lock. Read records with get_data. Decision records refuse data with decision_data_unsupported, decided records refuse it with decision_read_only, and legacy data stays readable.

Help: update_data, workspaces, tool-contracts, data.

name: list_docs
title: List documents

status.description: Only documents at this lifecycle state.

has_open_threads.description: Only documents with a known positive openThreadCount; topic rows match any live record. False refuses.

include_deleted.description: Include archived documents. Permanently deleted UUIDs are always excluded.

include_superseded.description: Return every decision record instead of one row per topic.

description:
List documents from this replica's directory, including local writes the hub has not acknowledged yet, without opening document rooms. Rows carry uuid, title, tags, description, updatedAt (ISO 8601 UTC when known and representable), openThreadCount (absent when unknown) and pinned. Unfiltered listings omit decisions; kind, status, tag and has_open_threads include them. A decision topic row shows the record in force, else pending, else first, with status, topic, discussion, answerPreview and inForce/pending/conflicts UUIDs. include_superseded lists every record; include_deleted adds archived rows (`deleted: true`). Filters combine; unknown tags refuse; has_open_threads accepts only true. get_doc reads code checks, threads and lifecycle details.

Help: list_docs, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions.

name: search
title: Search documents

query.description: Match any word in title, description, content, assigned tag names or code block languages, including English word forms. Case and accents fold; `release_plan` matches adjacent `release plan`, and a trailing * matches stem prefixes. A prefix past the stem can miss: `decisi*` can miss `decision`; search the whole word or a shorter prefix, `decis*`. Results use title-weighted bm25 relevance.

limit.description: Maximum hits, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20 after filters.

tag.description: One catalog tag id or name (case ignored), or a nonempty list. Match any listed tag; carrying more listed tags boosts relevance. Unknown tags refuse.

kind.description: Only regular documents (including stored requirements) or decision records, including superseded, rejected and withdrawn records.

description:
Find live documents containing any query word in titles, descriptions, content, assigned tag names or code block languages. English word forms match; case and accents fold, underscore groups match adjacent words and a trailing * matches stem prefixes. A prefix past the stem can miss: `decisi*` can miss `decision`; search the whole word or a shorter prefix, `decis*`. Punctuation or emoji alone matches nothing. Results use title-weighted bm25 relevance, without a strict title-first or matched-word-count order. Optional kind narrows to regular documents or decision records. Optional tag accepts one catalog id or current name (case ignored), or a list: any listed tag matches and more listed tags boost relevance; unknown tags refuse. Every hit includes kind and canonical tags; decision hits include current record state, including superseded and conflict. No hits does not prove the index is empty or the replica complete. If a needed page is missing, ask whether to create it.

Help: search, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions.

name: backlinks
title: Documents linking here
description:
Documents that reference this one, by UUID and never by path or title. The answer is the union of two kinds of edge, which it does not distinguish: the curated doc-level `links` set_metadata owns, and every inline reference in a prose block or table cell — written by link_range, an `inline` run, or a table cell's inline markdown. A citation needs no `links` entry to appear here.

Each one carries its `description` — null where it has none — so a citing document can be judged without opening it.

Help: backlinks, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: find_decisions
title: Find decisions linking a GitHub item

github_ref.description: One GitHub issue or pull request, as owner/repo#n or its github.com URL.

description:
Find live decision records whose prose links one GitHub issue or PR, using this replica's derived index without opening document rooms or calling GitHub. Only external link hrefs in prose count; labels, unlinked text and source blocks do not. Pass github_ref as owner/repo#n or an http(s) github.com /issues/n or /pull/n URL. Equivalent case/path spellings and suffixes normalize to the same identity; bare #n and other hosts refuse with invalid_github_reference. Returns every indexed live matching record once, ordered by title under SQLite binary collation then UUID, without pagination or topic resolution. Archived records are omitted. Results may lag unseen or unindexed content; an empty array does not prove replica completeness.

Help: find_decisions, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions.

name: edit_block
title: Edit one block

old_text.description: The block text you read. Asserted before the splice.

new_text.description: Replacement text. Repeat old_text to change only list style, depth, callout variant, icon or table column widths.

list.description: New list style on an existing list item; omitted keeps its style. Refused on other block types.

indent.description: New list depth, an integer from 0 to 3, on an existing list item; omitted keeps its depth. Refused on other block types.

variant.description: New callout variant: note, tip, important, warning or caution; omitted keeps it. Refused on other block types.

icon.description: New callout icon: one emoji character or a curated :name: icon; an empty value restores the default. Omitted keeps it. Refused on other block types.

rev.description: The block's `rev` from get_doc. Asserted alongside old_text.

table_mapping.description: Explicit surviving table positions. Both arrays are required; omitted old positions are deleted.

rows.description: For each new row, its old projection index or null; includes header row 0.

columns.description: For each new column, its old projection index or null.

column_widths.description: Tables only: one positive whole CSS-pixel width or null per table column. Null clears; omission keeps widths. Sizing guidance: markdown help.

description:
Change one block's text by diff-and-splice, so concurrent edits elsewhere in the block survive; a list item's `list` and `indent` can also change in place. Assert `old_text` and preferably the `rev` from get_doc: a mismatch refuses with stale_block or old_text_mismatch and returns currentText and currentRev to re-diff against. The assertion checks this replica only. A splice that touches a formatting mark's edge can re-anchor the mark, so check formatted text with export_markdown afterwards. An edit that would remove an open thread's last anchor refuses with open_thread_anchored; resolve the thread or move its anchor with annotate first. Tables take GFM and need `table_mapping` for structural or multi-cell edits; `column_widths` sizes columns (see markdown help). Card and Figma blocks take their `:::` content and cannot be converted to or from other types. New document-link targets must be known to this replica.

Help: edit_block, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown.

name: insert_block
title: Insert blocks

after_block_id.description: Insert after this block. Omit or null to insert first.

text.description: Plain prose (`inline` supplies formatting), literal code/terminal/chart source, exactly one GFM table, or :::card/:::figma content without delimiters. See markdown help for cell formatting, container keys, buttons and links. Invalid content refuses with invalid_table, invalid_card or invalid_figma before writing.

language.description: Code language, e.g. "ts". Code blocks only. Drawings are code blocks too, with language "ablauf" or "wireframe".

list.description: List style. List items only; omitted means bullet.

indent.description: List depth, an integer from 0 to 3. List items only; omitted means 0.

variant.description: Callout variant: note, tip, important, warning or caution; omitted means note. Ignored for other block types.

icon.description: Callout icon override: one emoji character or a curated :name: icon. Ignored for other block types.

inline.description: Prose (paragraph, heading, list-item, quote, callout) runs `[{text, marks}]`: marks are bold, italic, strike, inlineCode, link (external http(s) URL) or docLink (document UUID). Replaces `text` with joined run texts. Code, terminal and chart ignore it and use literal `text`; tables, cards and figma ignore it and parse inline Markdown from `text` (one GFM table or content inside :::card/:::figma). Empty docLink text takes the target's current title. A target unknown to this replica's directory refuses with doclink_target_not_known_locally before writing; archived targets are accepted.

column_widths.description: Tables only: one positive whole CSS-pixel width or null per table column. Null clears; omission keeps widths. Sizing guidance: markdown help.

blocks.description: Blocks to insert consecutively, in order. A single block is a one-entry array.

description:
Insert a nonempty blocks array consecutively after after_block_id, or at the top when omitted. Use the same entries as create_doc; one block is a one-entry array. Returns the new blocks in order, each with id and rev. Every entry is checked before anything is written: a refusal keeps its error code, names the 1-based entry_index and says nothing was written. Decision answers must keep their supported shape across the whole batch. Success sends one document update and moves the cursor once, to the end of the last inserted block's stored text. Lists use adjacent list-item entries with list/indent (default bullet/0). Container syntax lives in each entry's text field. Document-link targets must be known locally; chart source stays literal. Tables accept column_widths for immediate sizing. For column sizing, links and GitHub references, see markdown.

Help: insert_block, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown.

name: move_block
title: Move blocks

block_ids.description: Distinct block ids, in their destination order.

after_block_id.description: Move after this block. Omit or null to move first.

description:
Reorder existing blocks after after_block_id, or first when omitted/null, in block_ids order. Preserves ids, revs, content, attributes and comment anchors in one update; invalid moves write nothing. Concurrent edits or new comments on moved blocks before their replica receives the move are dropped, including offline edits.

Help: move_block, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown.

name: delete_block
title: Delete a block
description:
Delete one block. Deleting is never how a block changes type — use insert_block plus edit_block only for new content, and never delete-and-reinsert to re-type, which churns the block id and orphans its annotations. Refuses with open_thread_anchored if any open thread would lose its last document anchor. Use annotate to resolve that thread or move its anchor before deleting. Use move_block to reorder blocks.

Help: delete_block, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown.

name: set_metadata
title: Set document metadata together

title.description: Display title. A decision topic has one title stored on its first record; title on any live record renames the topic without changing answer approval. Successors take the topic's title.

description.description: Read only by agents, never shown to people: whatever best helps an agent find this document with list_docs and search and decide whether to open it. A keyword list is fine.

tldr.description: Person-facing regular-document summary, at most 300 characters. Null clears it without changing a deliberate removal mark. On a marked page, a non-null summary requires tldr_opt_in: true. Decisions have no TL;DR; open records accept null.

tldr_opt_in.description: Pass true with a non-null tldr to lift a person's deliberate TL;DR removal. Requires a non-null tldr; false does not lift the mark.

tags.description: The complete tag set, as existing catalog ids or names with case ignored. It replaces the current tags; [] clears them.

links.description: The complete curated link set. It replaces the current links; [] clears them. A new target must be known to this replica's directory; archived targets are accepted.

discussion.description: RFC discussion document UUID, or null to clear. Only an open decision record accepts changes; the target must be live, locally readable and not a decision. Distinct from curated links and the recorded answer; no document is created or tagged.

code_check.description: Record a regular page's latest comparison for one repository, replacing only that repository's entry. The writer sets checked_at to current UTC; callers do not supply it. Content edits leave checks unchanged.

repository.description: Repository as owner/name; identity ignores letter case.

result.description: matches: page describes this code; ahead: intended behavior is missing; drift: unintended disagreement.

rev.description: Page rev read with get_doc and compared with code; must still be current.

paths.description: Literal repo-relative files/folders looked at; trailing / marks folders. No leading /, .. segments or globs. Duplicates removed; hints, not complete dependencies.

description:
Change one or more of a document's title, description, TL;DR, tags, curated links and code check, or an open decision's discussion RFC. Name at least one field; omitted fields keep their values. The call is all or nothing: a refusal writes none of the named fields and names the failing `field`. Tags and links replace the whole set, and `[]` clears it. Title and description cannot be cleared; `tldr: null` clears the TL;DR. Decision records take no TL;DR or code check, and decided records also refuse discussion. Archived documents refuse every field; lifecycle status belongs to set_status.

Help: set_metadata, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions.

name: set_status
title: Set a document's lifecycle status

status.description: The recorded lifecycle state. Its kind owns the legal values.

when.description: When the person gave the answer: an ISO 8601 date-time with a time zone, e.g. 2026-10-24T10:55:00Z. Pass the current time if the answer was given just now.

where.description: Where the answer was given, such as a conversation or review URL.

answer.description: Record a person's answer, not the agent's own approval. MCP does not verify its provenance.

reason.description: Non-empty reason required when rejecting a proposal.

description:
Record a document's lifecycle status. On an ordinary document this also adopts the kind that owns the status; the result names both, so adoption is never silent. A document that already has a kind accepts only that kind's statuses. Its kind is fixed through MCP: if it was adopted in error, retrying with the other kind's status cannot change it. An open record can be withdrawn without an answer; decided records cannot reopen or withdraw. Rejected and withdrawn are final. Rejection requires a non-empty `reason` and a recorded person's answer, and applies only to an open proposal, an agent stance or a decided record in a conflict. It stores `rejectionReason`. Validation refusals change nothing.

Help: set_status, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions.

name: archive_doc
title: Archive a document
description:
Archive a document or every record of a decision topic, preserving content and UUID reads while hiding directory/search entries and unpinning. unpinned asserts the unpin, not whether a pin was found. An unseen concurrent pin may survive; get_sidebar shows it as archived and unpin_doc removes it. Restoration uses restore_doc and never re-pins. To delete an archived topic, call delete_doc with topic: true; one decision record cannot be deleted on its own yet. Directory/sidebar rooms persist independently without rollback. Results name rooms and indexed; persistence_failed names completed/failed rooms and recovery. Follow recovery before retrying.

Help: archive_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: delete_doc
title: Permanently delete an archived document

topic.description: True deletes every record of an archived decision topic, given its topic UUID or any record UUID; individual deletion is unavailable.

description:
Permanently delete an archived regular document, or with topic: true an archived decision topic given its topic UUID or any record UUID. Every topic record goes, including individually archived records. Deletes content, comments, data and history; only permanent UUID deletion evidence remains. Offline restores cannot undo it; replicas drop copies and the hub refuses rooms. Live topics/documents refuse with doc_not_archived; deleted UUIDs with doc_deleted. A decision UUID without topic: true refuses; one decision record cannot be deleted on its own yet. Other documents keep stored links. Directory/sidebar writes report independent durability.

Help: delete_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: restore_doc
title: Restore an archived document
description:
Remove one archive layer: restore an archived decision topic first, retaining records archived individually beforehand; in a live topic restore the addressed record. The archived result says whether that answer remains archived. Restore directory visibility and search indexing, using its recorded title and tags. It never restores a sidebar pin; use pin_doc for placement. On an already live regular document it can repair a drifted directory stub. Check indexed: false means this replica lacks the content or its index write failed. The restore still applies and replicates; search catches up when content arrives or a later call retries. Offline content arrival requires hub recovery.

Help: restore_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: annotate
title: Comment, reply, resolve, move or delete your comment

text.description: The comment body; required except when action is delete.

action.description: Permanent delete; requires thread_id/comment_id and forbids other mode fields.

comment_id.description: Delete only: stable id from get_doc or annotate.

thread_id.description: Reply to, move or delete a comment in this existing thread.

block_id.description: Target block for opening or moving an anchor.

row.description: Table cell row in the zero-based GFM projection, header 0.

column.description: Table cell column in the zero-based GFM projection.

resolved.description: Reply only: true resolves the thread; false reopens it.

description:
Open with block_id/start/end; reply with thread_id; move with thread_id plus block_id/start/end. These modes require text; author is optional. Only replies accept resolved to resolve or reopen. Moves replace all marks and keep the thread id, replies and resolution, including orphaned threads. Permanently delete with action: delete, thread_id and comment_id, without text or other fields. Yours means the stored account matches this session's signed-in GitHub account, ignoring case; no account means no delete. The opening comment removes the thread only while every reply is yours. Resolved comments cannot be deleted. Table targets need zero-based row/column, header 0; offsets count displayed characters and stored edge whitespace. Coordinates follow cells; orphaned ranges are null. Bad cell coordinates refuse with annotation_cell; empty or other-thread overlap ranges with annotation_range. Opening or moving into cards/Figma refuses with annotation_card/annotation_figma; their existing threads allow replies, resolution and moves to prose/table cells. See help for offset details.

Help: annotate, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown.

name: link_range
title: Link a range of a block to another document

rev.description: The block's `rev` from get_doc. Required, and asserted.

description:
Mark selected prose text as a document reference without changing its characters or rev. start/end are character offsets measured against the required rev; stale_block returns currentText/currentRev for remeasurement. Indices clamp to text and swap if reversed; empty ranges refuse. Existing document references are retargeted; external links, source blocks, tables, cards and Figma blocks refuse. Write card and Figma caption links as inline Markdown in their container text. doc_id must be known to this replica's directory or doclink_target_not_known_locally refuses before writing; archived targets are accepted. The answer includes the target title, but the label stays the selected text and does not follow renames. Backlinks update without changing curated meta.links.

Help: link_range, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown.

name: export_markdown
title: Export a document as markdown

frontmatter.description: Emit a YAML frontmatter block with uuid, title, tags and — when present — description, kind and status. The lifecycle fields record state; they do not authorize execution. Default true.

annotations.description: How to render annotation threads. Default drop.

description:
Render one document as read-only Markdown for reading, review or checking formatting. Markdown is never how documents are stored, and MCP has no Markdown import. The default frontmatter carries uuid, title, tags and, when set, description, kind and status; the TL;DR is not exported. Document links export as `[label](document-uuid)`. Comments are dropped unless `annotations` is `html-comments`, and structured data records are left out with a notice. Source blocks keep their fences, tables export as GFM, and cards and Figma blocks export as `:::` containers whose syntax markdown help gives.

Help: export_markdown, edit_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts, decisions, markdown, data.

name: sync_status
title: Sync status
description:
Inspect local replica state, pending rooms and hub connection/acknowledgements. hub.status distinguishes local, disabled, retryable hub-down, auth-failed requiring action, and update-required protocol mismatch. hub.recoveryClass, authRecovery and reason explain recovery; protocolVersion and hubProtocolVersion identify the incompatible side. Tools still work locally. unsyncedChanges counts durable pending rooms; inFlightUpdates counts provider sync messages on the current connection, resetting on reconnect. lastSync is this machine's stored UTC time when its full replica caught up, or null; it never moves backwards across processes. persistence diagnoses a failed log append and remains readable when ordinary replica tools are quarantined until restart. See this tool's help for counter units and lastSync conditions.

name: get_sidebar
title: Read the sidebar
description:
The workspace's curated navigation: named groups of pinned documents, in the order they are stored. This is not the corpus — unpinned documents are fully alive and reachable through list_docs, search, links and backlinks. Unpinned documents are simply not entry points.

Help: get_sidebar, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: pin_doc
title: Pin a document into a sidebar group

group.description: Group name, or the group id get_sidebar returned.

index.description: Position, clamped into range. Omitted means last.

description:
Pin a document into a group, creating the group when no group carries that name. `index` places it; omit it to append.

One pin per document across the whole sidebar, so this is also how a pinned document is moved or reordered: pinning one that is already pinned moves it to `index` in the named group — carrying the pin as it stands rather than re-pinning it, so a concurrent unpin still wins — and `index` then counts positions in the target group after the document has been taken out of it.

Help: pin_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: unpin_doc
title: Unpin a document
description:
Unpin without changing the document. archive_doc hides documents or topics; delete_doc permanently deletes archived documents or whole topics with topic: true. One decision record cannot be deleted on its own yet. Unpin beats concurrent moves; no group is needed because each document has at most one pin. unpinned:false means none existed. Empty groups remain; groupHint names sidebar_group to delete them.

Help: unpin_doc, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: sidebar_group
title: Rename, delete or move a sidebar group

action.description: What to do with the group.

group.description: Group name, or the group id get_sidebar returned.

name.description: The new name. rename only, and required there.

index.description: Position, clamped into range. Omitted means last.

description:
Manage the groups themselves. `delete` removes the group and its pins — the documents are untouched, because the group only ever held their uuids, and they stay reachable through list_docs and search.

`action` picks one of three shapes and each takes only its own field: `rename` needs `name` and refuses `index`, `move` takes `index` (omitted: last) and refuses `name`, `delete` takes neither. A field belonging to another action is refused at the input boundary before the sidebar is touched, rather than ignored — so a call that says two things is a failure you can see, not a silent half-success.

There is no create action: pin_doc creates a group by naming one that does not exist, which is how a group comes into being with something in it rather than empty.

Help: sidebar_group, workspaces, tool-contracts.
